title: Senior Allied Health Clinician: Review an Automated Summary Pilot
prompt: You are a senior allied health clinician reviewing a fictional summary-tool pilot. Supplied sample: source note says, "Person wants to explore returning to cooking; task performance not observed; partner available some evenings if asked." Generated handoff says, "Independent with cooking; partner provides daily support." The vendor reports 30% faster note completion in 10 volunteer users and recommends automatic handoff delivery. Exercise policy requires a clinician to verify every externally shared handoff against its source and the person's agreed sharing scope. Review the sample and propose a limited evaluation with clear stop conditions. No real records or live tool use is required.
blurb: Catch invented functional and support claims and design an evidence-based review of a documentation aid.

rubric.label: Identify unsupported clinical-adjacent statements
rubric.description: Tracks each summary claim to its source.

anchors.0: Accepts independence and daily support as paraphrases.
anchors.2: Flags both independence and daily support as unsupported.
anchors.4: Explains that a goal is not an observation and conditional availability is not an agreed daily commitment; rewrites both while preserving uncertainty and the person's goal.

rubric.label: Define an accountable review boundary
rubric.description: Keeps source verification and sharing decisions with a clinician.

anchors.0: Allows automatic handoff delivery after a generic disclaimer.
anchors.2: Requires clinician review against the original and sharing scope.
anchors.4: Defines claim-level comparison, explicit unknowns, correction traceability, a named reviewer and release gate, plus a way for the person to correct relevant support assumptions.

rubric.label: Evaluate benefit and failure together
rubric.description: Tests whether time savings survive verification and detects consequential errors.

anchors.0: Uses the 30% vendor estimate to justify broad deployment.
anchors.2: Measures error rates and review time in a limited pilot.
anchors.4: Defines sampled varied notes, unsupported/omitted claim categories, independent review with disagreement handling, total verified completion time, stop conditions for unreviewed sharing, and a bounded go/no-go owner.

reference.scenario: You are a senior allied health clinician reviewing a fictional summary-tool pilot. Supplied sample: source note says, "Person wants to explore returning to cooking; task performance not observed; partner available some evenings if asked." Generated handoff says, "Independent with cooking; partner provides daily support." The vendor reports 30% faster note completion in 10 volunteer users and recommends automatic handoff delivery. Exercise policy requires a clinician to verify every externally shared handoff against its source and the person's agreed sharing scope. Review the sample and propose a limited evaluation with clear stop conditions. No real records or live tool use is required.

facts.value: The 30% estimate measures drafting time only; it excludes review and corrections. No accuracy study or subgroup analysis was supplied.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks what the vendor measured

facts.value: The service can use 20 wholly fictional notes covering uncertain observations, changed goals, and conditional support. Two clinicians can independently review five overlapping cases.
A sandbox can prevent external delivery during the evaluation. The tool version can be recorded with each draft.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about containment or reproducibility

model_points: The example changes epistemic status twice: an aspiration becomes demonstrated independence, and conditional availability becomes a daily commitment. These errors can mislead a handoff even when prose sounds fluent.
Use the supplied mandatory verification boundary. A person's or partner's availability should not be invented, and only agreed sharing should leave the workflow.

The small volunteer drafting-time estimate excludes the work needed for a verified handoff. A fictional sandbox evaluation can measure errors and total effort with review disagreement and explicit release criteria.

probes.trigger: candidate says a clinician should proofread but gives no comparison method
probes.question: Which two source-to-summary changes should the review explicitly test?

probes.trigger: candidate recommends rejecting the tool without a pilot
probes.question: What evidence supports that decision, and what evidence would justify reconsideration later?

probes.trigger: candidate initially describes the person as independent then catches the source mismatch
probes.question: How would you correct both the summary and the pilot's error log?

fair_alternatives: Rejecting the current workflow or running a contained pilot are both defensible; neither needs to claim the technology is always unsafe or always useful.
Manual paired comparison is sufficient; no automated metric or programming is required.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess documentation evidence, service evaluation, and handoff governance. Do not judge functional capacity, prescribe therapy, or use real patient information. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess documentation evidence, service evaluation, and handoff governance. Do not judge functional capacity, prescribe therapy, or use real patient information. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Audit claim status
learning_drills.prompt: Mark each clause in the supplied summary as observed, reported, desired, conditional, or unsupported, then rewrite it. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
